diagram_math_checks.justification: Each panel is a (2,2) tangle, with two top inputs 1,2 and two bottom outputs 1-prime,2-prime as in the Statement and def-brauer-and-partition-diagram-categories. Tracing the arcs gives c1={{1,1-prime},{2,2-prime}}, c2={{1,2-prime},{2,1-prime}}, c3={{1,2},{1-prime,2-prime}}. These exhaust the three perfect matchings of four points, agreeing with F2 and the cardinality in step 18.1.

For the middle panel the first component starts at 1 and ends at 2-prime; the second starts at 2 and ends at 1-prime because 1<2<2-prime<1-prime. The 1-to-2-prime diagonal is drawn continuously through (3.2,.75); the other diagonal has a gap between (3.1,.6) and (3.3,.9). Thus the crossing is first met over, exactly the Statement definition and layer construction of step 3.1. It is deliberately not labeled a positive generator: step 8.3 states that positive right-over-left permutation lifts use the opposite auxiliary traversal.

Each panel has two simple arcs, no closed component, no self-crossing and no curl. The two noncrossing panels are descending vacuously. The separated top and bottom cup/cap curves in the third panel do not meet. These satisfy the representative conditions in the Statement and step 3.1; no additional curl coefficient, skein sign, isotopy equation, or commutative relation is asserted.

All original bytes through proof step 18.1 are retained exactly. The Remarks explicitly say the spanning, independence and isomorphism arguments remain independent of the illustration; steps 2.1, 3.1 and 4.1 supply those arguments without the new figure.
